This required input qualifies the native campaign profile of original 26FA40:
real character/vehicle policy selection, range and tracking-state ranks,
attention and recognition terms, extended-precision confidence, proximity and
player-relative motion alignment. The actual 266D30 and 26E040 callers consume
the scalar XMM0 result and store it in the tracked property at +3C.

The canonical gzip JSON is `native_campaign_ai_perception_score_tu15.json.gz`,
332,289 bytes; SHA256
`d020a0b4d3d4dd6af3a565665fd80bf71921f068e67ed0c219b62ba03f7aa6fb`.
It contains 334 complete unchanged physical original calls, one genuine
required-owner boundary and 479 retained-read failure prefixes. All 384 root
sites reachable in the admitted campaign/direct-mode private profile execute; 752 composed sites
execute overall. Exact complete physical banks are interned by SHA256 rather
than reconstructed from observed reads or writes.

One of the original 388 sites, 26FD81, is unreachable in the admitted serial
read-only profile: the entry requires signed property+24 > 0 and the same WORD
cannot become < 1 before its second check. The remaining three root sites are
the multiplayer call 26FE94 -> 160A60 and its 26FE99/26FE9C continuation. The
oracle stops at that genuine call, and the native code throws the corresponding
typed required-owner exception. It supplies no virtual team-policy result.
Campaign mode 1 instead follows the primary source's C1E90 bitset path using
team*16+1. Other direct modes are covered; generic multiplayer remains open.

Completed calls compare exact scalar bits and source x87/MXCSR controls and
sticky status. Cases cover all rounding modes, three x87 precisions, FTZ/DAZ,
finite and nonfinite values, paired NaNs with distinct payloads, real readonly
query/group/actor aliases, inherited authored policies and both motion-vector
paths. The native function preserves actual ambient host FP controls and live
x87 values. Its balanced confidence operation needs two private source x87
values, admitting zero through six occupied values with masked exceptions.
Unmasked traps and exhausted original stacks require their original owner.

All read failures compare exact lazy-read order, widths, values and unchanged
persistent banks; all compare source controls and SIMD status. Six failure
cases at confidence operand reads 26FDD8/26FDE2 do not claim original private
x87 temporary, TOP or partial arithmetic-status transport. Other read-failure
cases compare x87 status too. No guest FP stack or instruction machine is
constructed. Child-player output is the previously qualified disjoint private
pair; retained output aliases remain outside that profile.

The full caller consumes only backed declared tag/property references. Earlier
standalone character queries also return negative unbacked block identities;
those inputs are outside completed scoring calls, which dereference block+4.
The algorithm does not clamp their values or manufacture backing. Superseded
new input payloads were removed with compact hashes/reasons retained, including
the addition of the existing original policy table to observed retained banks.

`analysis/campaign-native-kernels-20261028/ai-perception-score/component-proof.json`
pins the exact independent physical repeat, GCC, Clang, six actual native
core/shared-helper ASan/UBSan objects and eight rejected semantic mutations.
`callers-and-profile.json` authenticates the real caller continuations,
campaign/multiplayer branch and unreachable-state invariant. Existing engine
owners already mount every numeric operand, including the 46A6D0 double.
The production module is `cmake/CampaignNativeAiPerceptionScore.cmake`.
Actual parent ABI/runtime composition, 264B50 alerts, 26E040 vision, full
unit-action begin and ai_set_orders remain separate gates. Offline original
executables, raw banks and builds are disposable and have been removed.
